How to Apply
How to Apply
Graduate study at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry means engaging in research and training that informs and shapes the world around us.
Located in western New York and integrated within a leading academic health system, our graduate programs emphasize personalized support and collaborative research opportunities. We invite you to explore our degree programs, our people, and our community. We welcome your application should you choose to apply!
Start Your Application PhD Frequently Asked Questions Master's Frequently Asked Questions
Applications for all graduate programs in the Department of Biostatistics and Computational Biology are accepted for matriculation in the Fall semester only. New students cannot start the PhD, Master of Arts, or Master of Science degree programs in the Spring.
How to Apply:
PhD Application Requirements
Master's Application Requirements
Applicant Checklist and Status Updates
Final Application Deadlines:
PhD Statistics - Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026; however, applications will be accepted until December 15, 2026
MA Statistics and MS Biostatistics - May 1, 2027
Application Fee Waivers:
PhD Statistics - The application fee is automatically waived for all PhD Statistics applications submitted by November 15. Please allow 90 minutes for the waiver to process after submitting the application. There is no code to enter.
MA Statistics and MS Biostatistics - The application fee is $60. If you previously completed a degree at the University of Rochester or are a current University of Rochester student, please contact Karin Gasaway for a manual application fee waiver. We cannot refund application fees.
Statistics and Biostatistics General Policies:
(a) GRE scores are no longer used by the Admissions Committee in evaluating applications to the program. If GRE scores are submitted, the committee will not look at them or take them into account when making admissions decisions.
(b) Most international applicants will need to provide TOEFL, IELTS, or DuoLingo English test scores unless they have earned or will earn an undergraduate baccalaureate degree from a U.S. educational institution (for automatic waiver) or from a country where English is an official language and all instruction is provided in English (manual waiver review). For consideration of any other waiver requests, including other graduate study in the United States, please email a copy of your most recent score report (even if expired) to Karin Gasaway.
